rooms.203059: The Gate Of The Inner City stands open in a deep arch of pale stone, its iron-shod leaves folded back against walls blackened by centuries of torch smoke. North through the arch, the Trade Road runs off between merchants' houses toward the wider realm. South, broad marble steps climb to the Temple of Garathorm, whose great dome fills the sky above the gate. A packed-earth yard opens west onto the training grounds, and a narrow stair in the gate tower climbs up to the wall-walk.
rooms.203006: Stalls of striped canvas crowd the top of the market square, their awnings snapping in the breeze and their keepers crying prices over one another. North, the square narrows toward the Temple Fountain, where the dome of the Temple rises white above the rooftops. The cobbles slope gently south into the middle of the square, while Inn Street opens east under a row of hanging signs. West, Alchemy Street slips away between tall houses that smell faintly of sulphur.
rooms.3036: Inn Street runs here beneath a long timber roof, a covered way built so that travellers could reach their beds dry in the worst of the rain. Lanterns hang from the rafters on chains, throwing warm light over flagstones scuffed by boots and barrel-rims. A carved gryphon over a doorway to the north marks the bar of the Gryphon's Rest Inn, and the post office stands south behind a counter window stacked with parcels. The covered way continues east, and west it opens onto the market square.
rooms.203007: Low beams blackened by pipe smoke hang over the bar of the Gryphon's Rest Inn, and a long oak counter, ringed by years of tankards, runs the length of the room. A painted gryphon spreads its wings across the wall behind the casks, its gilt flaking in places. Tables and settles crowd close around a fire that is never quite allowed to die. A door east leads through to the reception, and the way south returns to Inn Street.
rooms.3037: The covered length of Inn Street ends here at a broad crossing of passages under a roof of smoke-stained planks. A small arched doorway north climbs a few steps to the reception, where a bell can be heard ringing now and then. East, a heavy iron-banded door bears the city's crest and opens into the cityguards' barracks. South, the passage opens out toward The Main Street, and west the lantern-lit way runs back along the inns.
rooms.3038: Rows of narrow cots, each with a footlocker at its end, line the whitewashed walls of the cityguards' barracks. Halberds and round shields hang in racks by the door, polished and ready, and a duty roster is chalked on a board beside them. A doorway north lets in the clatter of the combat practice yard, and through a side door east drifts the damp, clean smell of Ye Olde Water Shoppe. The iron-banded door west leads back out to Inn Street.
rooms.203066: This walled yard of beaten earth is scored with the circles and lines of a hundred drills, and the ground is churned soft where boots have pivoted and lunged. Wooden pells stand along one side, hacked pale by blade after blade, and a water trough sits by the wall for the thirsty. North, a back door opens into the entrance hall of the Grunting Boar Inn, while a low shed east houses the dummy room. The barracks lie south, through a plain doorway under the open sky.
rooms.3084: Straw-stuffed dummies hang from hooks along the beams of this long, low shed, swaying slightly whenever the door is opened. Most have been beaten and restitched so many times that their sacking is more patch than cloth. Sawdust covers the floorboards to soak up sweat, and a single lantern burns behind a wire cage by the door. The only way out is west, back into the combat practice yard.
rooms.3067: An old gallows of weathered black timber stands on a stone platform in the middle of this square, unused for years but never taken down. Pigeons line its crossbeam, and the cobbles beneath it are stained darker than the rest. The Main Street lies north, and the ring of hammer on steel carries from the weapon shop east. South, a stout door opens into the entrance to the Warriors' Guild, while Council Avenue leads west.
rooms.3026: Council Avenue is the grandest street in this part of Garathorm, its cobbles laid in neat fans and its gutters swept clean each dawn. Banners of the city hang from tall poles along the way, stirring in the wind off the rooftops. North rise the columned steps of the Council Chamber, and south a moon gate in a whitewashed wall opens onto the Japanese Garden. East lies Gallows Square, and west the avenue runs down to the busy Southern End Of Market Square.
rooms.203069: Tiers of carved benches rise in a half-ring around a long table of dark walnut in the Council Chamber, where Garathorm's councillors meet to quarrel over the city's affairs. Tall windows of leaded glass let in a pale, even light, and the city's arms are worked in coloured stone upon the floor. A spiral stair behind the dais climbs up into the Marble Tower. The great doors south open onto Council Avenue.
rooms.203078: Polished white marble rises on every side in this high round room at the top of the Marble Tower Of Garathorm. Narrow windows set at intervals in the curving wall frame the rooftops, the city wall and the white dome of the Temple far below. A brass telescope on a stand points out through one of them, and a ring of cushioned benches follows the line of the room. The spiral stair winds back down to the Council Chamber.
rooms.3057: Raked gravel flows in careful ripples around mossy stones in this quiet walled garden, a gift, the gardeners say, from travellers who came from beyond the far sea. A little red bridge arches over a pond where lily pads drift, and a stone lantern stands by the water's edge. Through the moon gate north lies Council Avenue, and a plain wooden gate south lets out into the Eastern End Of Poor Alley. Harbour Square opens to the west past a stand of maples.
rooms.203026: Harbour Square smells of tar, river water and fish, and gulls wheel and cry over the slate roofs. A weathered bronze statue of a sea captain stands on a broad plinth at the west side of the square, a small dark opening half hidden at its base. North, the cobbles climb toward the Southern End Of Market Square, and east a whitewashed wall encloses the Japanese Garden. South, the square runs down to the stone edge of the Quay.
rooms.3034: Strange smells hang over this end of Alchemy Street, sulphur and burnt sugar and something sharp that stings the nose. North, a bow window crowded with glass bottles and coloured flames marks the magic shop, and west a doorway carved with runes opens into the entrance to the Mages' Guild. The street runs on east between leaning houses, and south it turns into Main Street. The gutters here run faintly blue and green with spilled reagents.
rooms.3035: Alchemy Street widens here between two of the most solid buildings in Garathorm. North stands the Garathorm Auction Hall, its doors hung with notices of lots to be sold, and south the Bank squats behind iron-barred windows and a door of studded oak. East, the street spills out into the bustle of the market square. West, it narrows among the alchemists' shops, where little coloured puffs of smoke rise from crooked chimneys.
rooms.203065: Rows of wooden benches face a raised platform in this echoing hall, where an auctioneer's lectern stands beside a heavy gavel block worn hollow in the middle. Chalk boards along the walls list lots, reserves and closing bids in a crabbed hand, many crossed out and written over. High windows let dusty shafts of daylight fall across the floorboards. The doors south lead back out onto Alchemy Street.
rooms.203077: Behind a long counter of polished marble, brass grilles divide the clerks' windows of the Bank from the public floor. The room is hushed, its stone walls thick and cool, and every footstep rings on the tiled floor. A great iron vault door, set with three locks and a wheel, fills the back wall behind the counter. The only way out is north, through the studded doors to Alchemy Street.
rooms.3056: Mismatched tables and chairs fill Uncle Juan's Eatery, a cramped little room whose walls are hung with strings of dried peppers and garlic. A great iron pot simmers on the hearth at the back, filling the air with the smell of beans, onions and spice. A slate by the counter lists the day's dishes in chalk, most of them cheap and all of them filling. The door south opens onto the Eastern End Of Dark Alley.
rooms.3039: A narrow path of trodden earth and broken cobbles runs along the river's edge here, between the water and the backs of tumbledown sheds. Reeds grow thick on the bank, and the slow brown river slides past carrying leaves and the odd bit of driftwood. East, the path firms into the stone of the Quay, while west a sour reek drifts up from the Dump. Overhead the sky is wide and open, smudged with chimney smoke.
rooms.203045: Great blocks of grey stone form the edge of the Quay, iron rings set into them for mooring and their faces green with weed where the river laps. Bollards, coiled hawsers and tarred posts clutter the wharf. Harbour Square lies north up a short slope, and the Quay runs on east along the water. South, the stone arch of a bridge leaps the river, and west a muddy path follows the bank away from the city.
rooms.3049: The far end of the Quay is quieter, its stones cracked and its bollards leaning. Wooden steps lead down from the edge of the wharf to the water south, where small boats can put out onto the river. A tall timber warehouse stands north, its loading doors and hoist beam looming over the stones. East, half hidden by a heap of rotting nets, a low dark opening in the old wall leads into a forgotten passage, and west the Quay runs back toward the bridge.
rooms.203050: Stacks of crates, bales and casks rise almost to the rafters of this great draughty warehouse, each marked in chalk with a merchant's sign. Narrow aisles run between them, and the air smells of tar, hemp and river damp. A hoist rope hangs from a beam above the wide doors to the south, which open onto the Quay. Pale light seeps in through gaps in the plank walls.
rooms.203074: The stone bridge arches high over the river here, its parapet worn smooth by the hands of countless leaning idlers. Below, the brown water swirls around the piers and carries the city's reflections away downstream. North, the bridge comes down onto the Quay among the warehouses, and south it descends to the Promenade on the far bank. Wind off the water tugs at cloaks and carries the cries of gulls.
rooms.203152: The Concourse runs here in the lee of the city wall, a broad way of flagstones where carts were once turned. The wall rises close by, grey and patched, its stones furred with moss in the cracks. The Concourse turns south along the wall, and west it leads back to the Northeast End Of The Concourse. East, the way bends round and seems to come back on itself, as the old streets of Garathorm sometimes do.
rooms.203153: The Concourse narrows here between the city wall and the blank backs of houses, and the flagstones give way to rough cobbles. Weeds push up along the foot of the wall, and a broken water butt leans beneath a rain-stained gutter pipe. North, the Concourse widens again, while a battered door south is set into a gap between two buildings, a hole in the wall that most passers-by never notice.
rooms.203154: This is little more than a gap knocked through the backs of two houses and roofed over with planks, a cramped hole in the wall barely wide enough for two to pass. The bricks are rough and crumbling, and water drips from the boards above into a puddle on the floor. A door north opens onto the Concourse, and another door south leads into the gloom of a dark alley.
rooms.203155: The dark alley here runs beneath overhanging upper storeys that meet overhead and shut out all but a grey crack of light. The walls are slick with damp and covered in thieves' marks scratched into the plaster. A rickety door west opens into a storage shed, and the alley creeps on south into deeper shadow. North, the way back leads to the hole in the wall.
rooms.3158: Refuse has piled up against the walls of this cramped stretch of the dark alley, and the smell of rot is thick under the low, sagging roof of beams. A single guttering lamp in an iron bracket gives off more smoke than light. West, a plank door hangs crookedly on its hinges at the mouth of a storage shed. The alley runs north toward the hole in the wall and south further into the dark.
rooms.3159: The alley narrows so sharply here that your shoulders brush the cold, sweating brick on both sides. Planks nailed across the gap overhead keep out the rain but trap every smell, and old straw rots in heaps underfoot. The way runs north toward the lamp-lit stretch of alley and south into a dead end of shadow.
rooms.3160: The dark alley comes to an end here against a blank wall of old stone, part of some forgotten building that Garathorm grew up around. Rusted hooks and the stub of an iron bracket jut from the bricks, and a heap of broken barrel staves fills the corner. It is very quiet, the noise of the city reduced to a far murmur beyond the roof. The only way out is north, back along the alley.
rooms.3157: Shelves of rough planking line the walls of this cramped storage shed, bowed in the middle from years of heavy loads now long gone. The single window is boarded over, and thin bars of grey light fall through the gaps onto a floor of packed earth. The place smells of mould and old sacking. A plank door east lets back out into the dark alley.
rooms.3156: This storage shed is a little larger than its neighbours, built of tarred boards under a roof that leaks in one corner. Empty crates have been stacked into a rough wall, and someone has chalked tallies and strange signs on the boards above them. Damp has blackened the floor along one side where the rain gets in. A door east opens back into the dark alley.
rooms.206400: Tall bronze doors stand open on the west side of this vaulted entryway, letting in the noise of Penny Lane and a wash of daylight that fades quickly on the cool stone floor. Within, the air is hushed and smells of incense and candle wax. Seven gods are carved in a frieze above the inner arch, each gazing down the long hall that runs east to their chapels. A basin of holy water stands by the door for those who enter.
rooms.206401: A long hallway of pale grey stone runs through the temple here, its ceiling lost in shadow high above. Iron candle-stands line both walls, their flames steady in the still air, and worn runners of red carpet muffle every step. East, the hallway opens into a crossing where the first chapels lie, and west the way leads back to the entryway and its bronze doors.
rooms.206402: Here the hallway meets its first pair of chapels, their arched doors facing each other across the flagstones. North, an arch wreathed in carved flowers and vines opens into the Chapel of Livana, while south a doorway framed in dark iron leads into the Chapel of Eranohk. The hallway runs on east beneath a row of hanging lamps, and west back toward the entryway.
rooms.206403: Green light falls through a window of stained glass into the small Chapel of Livana, where living vines have been trained up the walls and across the vaulted ceiling. A low altar of white stone holds bowls of seeds and fresh blossoms, and the air smells of earth and spring. Carved into the face of the altar, a woman with flowing hair holds a sheaf of wheat. The arched door south returns to the temple hallway.
rooms.206404: Iron rules the stern Chapel of Eranohk: iron sconces, an iron-bound altar, and old shields and swords hung in rows upon the walls as offerings. The stone floor is scarred where worshippers have knelt in armour, and a red lamp burns before a statue of a bearded warrior leaning on a great axe. The air is cold and smells of oil and steel. The iron-framed doorway north leads back into the hallway.
rooms.206405: The hallway runs on through the heart of the temple, and the sound of distant chanting drifts along its vaulted length. North, a doorway painted deep blue and spangled with silver stars opens on the Chapel of Quaralin, and south a door carved with rolling waves leads into the Chapel of Veranalla. More chapels lie east along the hall, and west it returns toward the entryway.
rooms.206406: Deep blue paint covers the domed ceiling of the Chapel of Quaralin, scattered with silver stars set out in the true shapes of the constellations. Shelves of scrolls and star charts line one wall, and a bronze orrery of turning spheres stands upon the altar. A few cushioned stools wait for those who come to study or pray in silence. The starry doorway south opens back onto the hallway.
rooms.206407: The Chapel of Veranalla is cool and echoing, its walls tiled in blue and green like the depths of the sea. A broad basin of water sits where the altar would be, fed by a thin trickle from a carved shell in the wall, and its gentle sound fills the room. Ropes, oars and little carved boats hang on the walls, left in thanks by sailors who came home. The wave-carved door north leads back into the hallway.
rooms.206409: The temple hallway grows dimmer here, the candle-stands set further apart and the shadows thicker between them. North, a door painted in cheerful patches of yellow and red leads into the Chapel of Jojeebe, and from it comes the faint chime of bells. South, a plain black door marks the Chapel of Zirande, silent and cold. The hallway continues east toward the sanctuary and runs west back the way you came.
rooms.206410: Bright patchwork hangings drape the walls of the Chapel of Jojeebe, and strings of tiny brass bells hang from the ceiling, chiming at the faintest draught. The altar is a round table painted like a gaming board, its rim carved with dice and grinning masks. A smiling statue of a jester with a cup raised in a toast stands behind it. The patched door south leads back to the hallway.
rooms.206411: The Chapel of Zirande is dark and very still, lit only by a single grey candle in a recess behind the altar. Black hangings cover the walls, embroidered with silver owls and the shapes of closed eyes. Upon the plain stone altar lies a carved figure of a hooded woman, her hands folded over a key. Every footstep sounds too loud here, and the black door north opens back into the hallway.
rooms.206413: The hallway ends here before a pair of tall gilded doors that open east into the Temple Sanctuary, and a golden light spills through them onto the floor. North, a doorway hung with soft white curtains leads into the Chapel of Miylorei, and the scent of lavender drifts out from it. Tapestries of the seven gods line the walls, and the hallway runs back west past the other chapels.
rooms.206412: Soft white curtains and a sweet smell of lavender fill the gentle Chapel of Miylorei, goddess of healing and mercy. Low cots stand along one wall for the sick who come to pray, and bundles of dried herbs hang from the beams above them. On the altar a marble statue of a young woman holds out her open hands, the stone of her palms worn smooth by countless touches. The curtained doorway south leads back to the hallway.
rooms.206408: The Temple Sanctuary is a high, round chamber beneath a gilded dome, lit by a ring of windows that pour golden light down onto a great altar of white marble. Seven tall candles burn upon it, one for each god of the temple, and they never seem to gutter. The floor is inlaid with a great sun of gold and amber stone, and rows of kneeling benches face the altar. The gilded doors west lead back to the hallway.
rooms.206700: Bazaar Street begins here where it leaves Emerald Avenue, and at once the air fills with the cries of hawkers and the smell of spice and roasting nuts. Coloured awnings stretch from house to house overhead, turning the daylight into a patchwork of red and saffron. The street runs east into the heart of the bazaar, and west it opens onto the quieter cobbles of Emerald Avenue.
rooms.206701: Two shopfronts face each other across this stretch of Bazaar Street. North, Imrik's Shop hangs out a crooked wooden sign beside a dusty bow window, while south, Ruby's Shop glitters behind small panes of red glass. The cobbles here are strewn with straw and trodden fruit, and a tinker's bell clangs somewhere along the street. The bazaar continues east, and west it leads back toward Emerald Avenue.
rooms.206702: Imrik's Shop is a narrow, cluttered room where shelves climb all the way to the ceiling, reached by a ladder that slides along a rail. A long counter scarred by knives and coins divides the shop, and a brass scale stands at one end of it. Lamps of every shape hang from the beams, though only a few are ever lit. The shop door south opens onto Bazaar Street.
rooms.206704: The bazaar grows louder here, the street hemmed in by trestles and barrows that spill out from the shops. North, Jelloz's Shop is painted a startling shade of green, and south the dark doorway of Sargoth's Shop is flanked by a pair of carved wooden wolves. A public fountain of chipped stone stands in a recess in the wall, its spout shaped like a lion's head. The street runs on east and west through the market din.
rooms.206705: Every wall of Jelloz's Shop is painted the same bright green as its front, and the shelves are stacked with stoppered jars of every size. The air is sweet and sticky, smelling of sugar and preserved fruit. A long counter of green-stained wood runs across the room, with a little brass bell upon it for summoning service. The door south leads back out onto Bazaar Street.
rooms.206707: Here Bazaar Street turns a corner, and the din of the market eddies around it like water round a stone. East, Silvina's Shop shows a narrow front of silver-grey stone with a delicate sign of a crescent moon. South, Akaniz's Shop is half hidden behind a curtain of hanging rugs and brass lamps. The street bends north between the stalls and runs back west through the bazaar.
rooms.206710: A stone archway spans the street here, so old that its carvings have worn to vague, friendly lumps. East, Cardini's Shop is fronted by a striped awning and a board chalked with the day's bargains, while west the door of Bedlamzer's Shop is painted with whirling spirals that make the eye swim. The cobbles rise gently north under more awnings and fall away south to the bend in the street.
rooms.206713: Bazaar Street climbs a short slope here, and the stalls give way to proper shopfronts with glazed bow windows. East, Palaon's Shop is neat and freshly whitewashed, its brass door handle polished bright. West, Erraticus's Shop leans at a curious angle, its shutters hanging crooked and smoke of an odd violet hue curling from its chimney. The street continues north toward Merchant Avenue and south back down through the bazaar.
rooms.6716: The bazaar ends here where Bazaar Street meets the wider cobbles of Merchant Avenue, which opens east between the tall houses of wealthy traders. North, a heavy door studded with nails marks Shagrat's Shop, and west, Rhinocreed's Shop announces itself with a great carved horn mounted above the lintel. A worn stone mounting block stands at the corner. South, the awnings of the bazaar crowd down the slope of the street.

203007.description: The gryphon is painted rampant in gold and russet, its beak open in a silent cry. Someone long ago added a tankard to one of its claws in a clumsier hand, and no landlord since has had the heart to paint it out.

3067.description: The gallows has not been used in living memory. Its rope is long gone, and the iron hook on the crossbeam has rusted to a dull brown stump.

3057.description: The lantern is a squat pagoda of grey granite, its little roof furred with moss. A candle is lit inside it each evening, and its light trembles on the pond.

203077.description: The vault door is as tall as two men and blackened with age. Its three locks each take a different key, and the great wheel at its centre is polished bright by the clerks' hands.

206400.description: The seven gods of the temple stand shoulder to shoulder in the frieze: Livana with her wheat, Eranohk with his axe, Quaralin crowned with stars, Veranalla rising from a wave, Jojeebe laughing, Zirande hooded and Miylorei with open hands.

206406.description: Seven bronze spheres hang on slender arms around a golden sun. A small crank at the base turns them, and the priests say it shows the heavens as they truly move.

206408.description: The candles are as thick as a man's arm and never seem to grow shorter. Each is a different colour, one for each of the seven gods, and their flames burn straight and still.
